card.name: Word 'use' after Concomitant; 'to' after due
card.fires_on: The word "use" right after "Concomitant" in drug-interaction headings, and "to" in "contraindicated due to". It sits just before a named drug or an interaction reason.

modes.label: Concomitant use
modes.description: "use" following "Concomitant" at the start of an interaction statement about enzyme inhibitors or inducers.
modes.example: 450 3A4 Inhibitors and Inducers Concomitant<< use>> of Hydrocodone Bitartrate

modes.label: Due to
modes.description: "to" after "due" when giving the reason a co-administered drug is contraindicated.
modes.example: rifampin is contraindicated due<< to>> potential for loss of elvitegrav

card.plain: It marks the point in a drug-interaction statement where the drug name or the reason for the restriction comes next.
